node.title: Re^3: Prototype mismatch: sub main::trim: none vs ($)
node.author: Marshall
node.doctext:
As a nit, [http://perldoc.perl.org/perlfaq4.html#How-do-I-strip-blank-space-from-the-beginning/end-of-a-string%3f | Perl FAQ trimming spaces] says that running both the 2 regex'es above (ltrim and rtrim) is faster than the single regex trim. This post on StackOverflow [http://stackoverflow.com/questions/2313879/why-is-s-s-s-g-so-much-slower-than-two-separate-substitutions | Why is single regex slower?] goes into more detail about exactly why that is true.

These 2 lines are such an idiom that I just type them from memory without needing to use a sub. With Perl, not every "shorter" formulation is faster.
